title: Consolidated Technical Debt Register — Framework v2 Stewardship Baseline

learner_safety.description: Defects that affect items currently in the Certified learner delivery pool. These are the highest priority — learners may encounter degraded educational feedback or incorrect content.

items.title: Metadata-Block ChoiceA-D +1 Offset on Certified Items
items.scope: Pack A Sections B, C, F (Certified). Possible Pack C/D dual-block sections.
items.impact: Metadata ExplanationWrong fields describe the wrong item's distractors. Learners selecting wrong answers on affected Certified items see explanations about a different topic. Educational feedback is misleading.
items.current_state: Pack A Section E remediated S805 (57 items). Pack A Sections B/C/F remain. Pack C/D dual-block status not yet confirmed.
items.effort: Medium — requires per-item metadata/content alignment, ≤30 items per batch
items.target: Before any further Pack A/C/D certification waves
items.remediation_path: Align metadata-block ChoiceA-D and ExplanationWrongA-D with content-block Choices.A-D. Verify per-item that EW text corresponds to the item's actual distractors.

items.title: 39 Domain F Certified Items with Empty Distractor ExplanationWrong Slots
items.scope: 39 items: Pack C (28 Domain F) + Pack D (11 Domain F). ~117 empty non-CC ExplanationWrong fields.
items.impact: Learners who select wrong answers on these items see no educational feedback. Content correctness is unaffected (zero DL-008). Educational quality is degraded.
items.current_state: Identified S812. Rule 6 deployed S814 (prevention). Content remediation scheduled S816-S818.
items.effort: Medium — author ~117 choice-specific distractor explanations, ≤30 items per batch
items.remediation_path: Author choice-specific ExplanationWrong fields for all empty non-CC slots. Technology & Analytics domain-appropriate content. 4 batches ≤30 items per Rule 5.

quality_systematic.description: Defects that affect large numbers of items across multiple packs. These are systematic quality issues from template-based authoring — not learner-safety critical but significantly impact the quality of non-Certified content.

items.title: Systematic Difficulty Inflation — Definition-Match Items
items.scope: ~500 items across all 5 packs. Items where stem is a textbook definition and answer is the defined term, labeled Moderate that should be Easy.
items.impact: Difficulty distribution does not match CAQS §6.1 targets. Psychometric calibration is unreliable. Adaptive learning and study planning based on difficulty are compromised.
items.current_state: Scoped by Session 700 Layer 2. Not remediated. Scope estimates: Pack A ~100, Pack B ~200, Pack C ~100, Pack D ~100, Pack E ~50.
items.effort: High — requires per-item cognitive assessment and difficulty recalibration across ~500 items
items.target: Before any new difficulty-dependent features are deployed
items.remediation_path: Per-item cognitive assessment. Recalibrate definition-match items from Moderate→Easy where confirmed. Verify Bloom's level alignment with difficulty label. Target CAQS §6.1 distribution post-recalibration.

items.title: Case Bank Uniform Difficulty — Zero Variance
items.scope: ~330 case items across scored_cases2-5. All labeled 'Moderate' with no variance. ENHANCED_CASE_BASE (scored_cases.js, 90 items) already remediated S530/S537.
items.impact: All case items have identical difficulty. Psychometrically implausible for 330 items across 6 domains. Adaptive learning and study planning compromised.
items.current_state: 60 cases (330 items) in scored_cases2-5 still uniform. 15 cases (90 items) in scored_cases.js remediated.
items.effort: Medium-High — per-item difficulty assessment across 330 items
items.target: Before case items enter certification pipeline
items.remediation_path: Assign genuine difficulty labels based on cognitive level, calculation complexity, exhibit dependencies, and distractor deceptiveness. Target CAQS §6.1 distribution.

content_backlog.description: Structural and content defects in non-Certified items. These block certification but have zero learner pool impact (items are Unprocessed or In Audit).

items.title: Pack C/D Section E Clonal Redundancy — 140 Template Clones
items.scope: 140 clone items across Pack C Section E (EC-001–EC-075) and Pack D Section E (ED-001–ED-075). 28 clone groups × 5 items each. 10 standalone unique items.
items.impact: 140 items provide zero additional pedagogical value beyond the 28 seed items. Clones dilute population metrics and distort blueprint coverage reporting. Decision pending: archive vs. re-key with UniqueConceptKey.
items.current_state: Documented in DL-012. Remediation proposal exists (DL012_REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL.md) but not executed. Pack C/D are BLOCKED from edit per SESSION_STATUS.
items.effort: Low-Medium — decision + mechanical archival or re-keying
items.target: After DL-008/DL-026 resolution on Pack C/D
items.remediation_path: Option A (Archive): mark 112 clones as Archived, keep 28 seeds active. Option B (Re-key): assign unique UniqueConceptKey to distinguish genuinely independent items. See DL012_REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL.md for full comparison.

items.title: Template Boilerplate Distractor Explanations — 851 Fields Remaining
items.scope: 851 ExplanationWrong fields across 366 QIDs. Pack A (238 fields, 94 QIDs), Pack C (357 fields, 159 QIDs), Pack D (256 fields, 113 QIDs). All non-Certified.
items.impact: Distractor explanations say 'represents a plausible misconception' instead of explaining why the distractor is wrong. Zero learner pool impact (all items non-Certified). Blocks certification of affected items.
items.current_state: 1,736 of 2,587 fields cleared (67.1%). Remaining 851 fields deferred to certification waves.
items.effort: High — requires rewriting ~851 distractor explanations, ≤30 items per batch
items.remediation_path: Rewrite boilerplate ExplanationWrong fields to be choice-specific. Replace 'represents a plausible misconception... A candidate may select this option by misapplying a related but distinct concept' with specific misconception identification and correction. Per-section approach alongside certification.

architectural_gaps.description: Gaps between Framework v2's intended design and current implementation. These are process/infrastructure items, not content defects.

items.title: Pipeline Artifact Reuse — Zero Downstream Consumption
items.scope: Certification pipeline — scan orchestrator, readiness scorer, certification candidate engine. Currently each independently re-scans raw files.
items.impact: 40-item BLOCKED routing divergence (DL-036). Redundant computation. Risk of divergent methodology producing conflicting results.
items.current_state: Identified S812. Documented in DL-036. Scheduled S819-S820 (S813 C2).
items.effort: Medium — connect existing pipeline stages via artifact consumption
items.remediation_path: Connect scan orchestrator output → readiness scorer input → certification candidate engine input. Eliminate independent re-scanning. Single source of truth for per-item classification.

items.title: Student Performance Data — Design Ready, Zero Operational Data
items.scope: Canonical student record schema (v1.0.0) designed. Data source inventory complete. Import/export contracts specified. Zero operational student data exists.
items.impact: Student Exposure Index (S254: 80/100, DATA_GAP) cannot operate. Adaptive learning features cannot be validated. All student-facing analytics are blocked.
items.current_state: Design complete (S255). Architecture ready. No production deployment exists.
items.effort: None for architecture — requires production deployment
items.remediation_path: Deploy to production. Student data will flow through the designed bridge. Architecture is complete — this is a deployment gap.

items.title: No Production Deployment — All Validation at Build/Development Level
items.scope: Entire CMA Part 1 Exam Simulator. All certification, validation, and testing has been at build/development level.
items.impact: Runtime performance, browser compatibility, loading behavior, and production-level crash scenarios are untested. The DL-022 crash guard fix (null-session restore) was developed from simulated localStorage corruption — not from observed production crashes.
items.current_state: S207 operational certification certified infrastructure stability. No production deployment has occurred.
items.target: Production deployment (separate from content debt remediation)
items.remediation_path: Production deployment. Monitor runtime behavior. Feed production observations back into defect detection.

legacy_artifacts.description: Files, directories, and data that exist from pre-Framework v2 era and should be cataloged, archived, or linked.

items.title: Report File Proliferation — ~1,227 Files, 65% Unconsumed
items.scope: ~1,227 report files (843 JSON, 372 MD) across reports/ directory. Produced across 178 sessions.
items.impact: Discovery burden — finding the authoritative report on any topic requires searching hundreds of files. Wasted agent effort on one-off reports.
items.current_state: S201 Board 5 documented the scale. No archival or cataloging performed.
items.remediation_path: Catalog all 1,227 files by session, type, and consumption status. Archive one-off reports. Link consumed reports to consuming tools/registries. Apply DRIFT-5 detection at session closeout going forward.

items.title: Backup File Accumulation — Multiple Generations of .bak Files
items.scope: Dozens of .bak files in project root (pack_*_corrected.js.bak-*, may-core.js.bak-*, scored_cases*.js.bak-*, etc.) spanning multiple session generations.
items.impact: Clutters project root. Backup management is inconsistent (some in backups/, most in root).
items.current_state: Per BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md, backups are created before edits. Old backups are not systematically cleaned up.
items.effort: Low — reorganize or archive old backups
items.remediation_path: Move old .bak files to backups/archive/. Keep recent backups (last 2 sessions) in root. Establish backup retention policy.

items.title: Pack B and Pack E Hash Drift — Post-S811 Authorized Changes Without Updated Baselines
items.scope: pack_b_corrected.js (SHA-256: 1951D387... vs baseline 8A641309...) and pack_e_corrected.js (SHA-256: B5E954D3... vs baseline A98B27B1...). Both have today's backups confirming post-S811 modifications.
items.impact: CURRENT_BASELINES.md is stale for 2 of 15 runtime files. Baseline verification at T0 would fail. Content integrity is preserved (backups exist) but traceability is degraded.
items.current_state: Detected S208 T0. Backups exist: pack_b_corrected.js.bak-20260727151912, pack_e_corrected.js.bak-20260727151913.
items.effort: Low — recapture hashes and update CURRENT_BASELINES.md
items.target: Next session with write authorization for knowledge/CURRENT_BASELINES.md
items.remediation_path: Recapture SHA-256 hashes for Pack B and Pack E. Verify content integrity (parse, QuestionID count). Update CURRENT_BASELINES.md §1. Investigate what changed (check REVISION_HISTORY.md for post-S811 entries).
